full_prompt_html:
Act as an information security officer, a third-party risk analyst and a data protection specialist.

We are about to sign with a software vendor that will handle our data. Review the vendor’s security answers and tell us whether it is safe to proceed. [Paste the vendor’s completed security questionnaire, SOC 2 report summary or security documentation.] [Describe what data the vendor will access and how your staff will use the service.]

Assess the vendor in four areas:

1. Evidence Quality

  • For each answer, state whether the vendor gives evidence (a certification, an audit report or a named control) or only a statement.
  • Flag vague answers, such as “industry-standard security”, that do not describe a control.
  • Note any certification that has expired or does not cover the service we are buying.

2. Data Protection

  • Check where our data is stored and processed, who at the vendor can access it, and how it is encrypted at rest and in transit.
  • Identify how the vendor uses customer data, including whether it trains AI models on it, and which subprocessors it relies on.
  • Confirm how our data is returned and deleted when the contract ends.

3. Access and Incident Response

  • Assess support for single sign-on, multi-factor authentication and role-based access.
  • Check the vendor’s breach notification timeline and whether it meets our contractual or regulatory obligations.

4. Risk Rating and Conditions

  • Rate the vendor as low, medium or high risk for the data described, and give the main reason.
  • List the conditions we should require before signing, such as contract clauses or configuration settings.
  • List the follow-up questions for the vendor.

Deliver a one-paragraph verdict first, then a table with columns for Area, Finding, Evidence, Risk and Required Action, followed by the follow-up questions. Where the documents do not answer a point, mark it as unanswered.
summary: Review a vendor’s security answers for evidence quality, data storage and AI training use, access controls, breach notification, and overall risk.
title: Check a vendor’s security answers before you sign
